collection: Primary4 Igbo limited numerical language and operation reasoning
note: Thirteen original structured drafts: eleven written, one live/recorded spoken sequence and one observed object-counting task. Seven partial source mappings within50; unresolved fifty-versus-500 range, source sound notation and unit terminology remain open. All academic/native review pending.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Use Igbo numbers to count actual objects within an explicitly limited 1–50 subset.
questions.prompt: Gụọ mkpụrụ mgbakọ onye nkụzi debere n’ihu gị. Metụ nke ọ bụla aka otu ugboro mgbe ị na-agụ ha n’Igbo. Kwuo ole ha dị mgbe ị gụchara.
questions.answer: Teacher-only setup: exactly11 counters. Learner counts every counter once in intelligible Igbo and states the total: iri na otu. Actual performance is required; this written key is not observation evidence.
questions.explanation: One-to-one counting and naming the resulting quantity are assessed separately. No counter image, learner performance or audio is claimed.

markingGuide.description: Counts each of the11 counters once without omitting or recounting one.
Uses an intelligible correctly ordered Igbo counting sequence.
States the final quantity as11 in Igbo; illustrative form iri na otu.

questions.scopeLimitation: Limited original practice with all quantities at most50. Does not resolve source fifty-versus-500 conflict, establish full1–500 coverage, local adoption, official term placement or actual classroom performance.
questions.teacherSupport: Before use, a native Igbo examiner checks number forms and instructions. Set exactly11 safe large counters, separated and visible. Observe the individual learner pointing/counting and stating the total; retain an observation record under school policy. Do not substitute the model answer or a hypothetical display for performance.
questions.deliveryNote: Requires actual objects and witnessed counting. No live activity occurred during authoring.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Use Igbo numbers to count actual objects within an explicitly limited 1–50 subset.
questions.prompt: Akwụkwọ asaa dị n’elu tebụl. E dozigharịrị ha ka ha bụrụ ahịrị abụọ; e tinyeghị akwụkwọ ọzọ, e wepụghịkwa nke ọ bụla. Ha ka dị ole? Kọwaa ihe mere nhazi ọhụrụ ahụ anaghị agbanwe ọnụọgụgụ ha.
questions.answer: Ha ka dị asaa. Naanị nhazi ha gbanwere; e tinyeghị akwụkwọ ọzọ, e wepụghịkwa nke ọ bụla.
questions.explanation: The learner explains conservation of a counted set under rearrangement, rather than assuming that a longer row contains more objects.

markingGuide.description: States asaa/seven in Igbo.
Explains in intelligible Igbo that rearrangement changes positions but neither adds nor removes books.

questions.learningObjective: Count aloud in Igbo within an explicitly limited 1–50 subset.
questions.prompt: Bido n’iri abụọ, gụọ n’olu n’Igbo ruo iri abụọ na ise. Kwụsị mgbe ị ruru ọnụọgụgụ ikpeazụ ahụ.
questions.answer: Illustrative sequence: iri abụọ; iri abụọ na otu; iri abụọ na abụọ; iri abụọ na atọ; iri abụọ na anọ; iri abụọ na ise. Equivalent locally checked forms are acceptable.
questions.explanation: This is an actual oral sequence task with defined endpoints; written recitation is insufficient. It is a small interval, not evidence of counting1–500.

markingGuide.description: Starts with20 and continues in the correct order through22, in intelligible Igbo.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Write ordinary numerals and corresponding Igbo names within an explicitly limited 1–50 subset.
questions.prompt: Chidi dere 42 maka okwu “iri abụọ na anọ”. Ọ bụ eziokwu? Dee akara ọnụọgụgụ kwesịrị ekwesị, deekwa 42 n’okwu Igbo iji gosipụta ọdịiche ahụ.
questions.answer: Mba. Iri abụọ na anọ bụ24. 42 bụ iri anọ na abụọ.
questions.explanation: The learner distinguishes tens from units in written language; reversing the digits changes the named quantity.

markingGuide.description: Rejects42 as the numeral for iri abụọ na anọ and writes24.
Writes an intelligible Igbo name for42: iri anọ na abụọ.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Explain addition and subtraction in intelligible Igbo using concrete quantities within 50.
questions.prompt: Jiri ihe atụ pensụl kọwaa mgbakọ na mwepụ n’Igbo. Malite na pensụl ise: gịnị na-eme n’ọnụọgụgụ ha ma e tinye abụọ ọzọ? Gịnị na-eme ma e wepụ abụọ n’ime ise ahụ?
questions.answer: Mgbakọ bụ itinye ihe ọnụ:5+2=7, pensụl asaa. Mwepụ bụ iwepụ ụfọdụ n’ihe e nwere:5−2=3, pensụl atọ fọdụrụ.
questions.explanation: Both operations start from the same original five. The subtraction is not performed on the result of the addition; the learner must explain the different actions.

markingGuide.description: Explains in Igbo that addition joins/adds quantities.
Gives5+2=7 and names the total in Igbo.
Explains in Igbo that subtraction removes from the starting quantity.
Gives5−2=3 and names the remainder in Igbo.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Relate Igbo addition and subtraction expressions to their signs and interpret equality within 50.
questions.prompt: E nwere iko iri na abụọ. E wepụrụ iko anọ. Otu nwa dere 12 + 4 = 16 iji kọwaa ihe mere. Kedu akara na nsonaazụ kwesịrị ekwesị? Jiri okwu Igbo kọwaa ihe mere i ji họrọ akara ahụ.
questions.answer: 12−4=8. E ji akara mwepụ mee ihe n’ihi na e wepụrụ iko anọ; iko asatọ fọdụrụ.
questions.explanation: The printed addition statement is arithmetically true but does not model the described removal. This assesses operation-language choice, not merely rejecting any equation containing16.

markingGuide.description: Replaces+ with−.
Gives the correct equation12−4=8.
Explains the removal meaning in intelligible Igbo.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Relate Igbo addition and subtraction expressions to their signs and interpret equality within 50.
questions.prompt: Dee akara kwesịrị ekwesị n’ebe oghere dị: 9 + 6 __ 10 + 5. Kọwaa n’Igbo ihe akara ahụ na-egosi banyere akụkụ abụọ ahụ.
questions.answer: 9+6=10+5. Akụkụ abụọ ahụ bụ iri na ise; akara= na-egosi na ha ha nhata.
questions.explanation: Equality expresses the same value on both sides, even when both sides contain calculations. It does not simply mean that an answer must follow on the right.

markingGuide.description: Uses the equals sign.
Explains in intelligible Igbo that both sides represent the same quantity,15.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Use multiplication and division symbols for equal groups and equal sharing within 50, explaining their meaning in Igbo.
questions.prompt: E nwere efere anọ, iko atọ dị n’efere ọ bụla. Dee mgbakọ a site n’iji akara ×. Gwa anyị n’Igbo ihe 4, 3 na nsonaazụ ya na-anọchi anya. Gịnị mere 4 + 3 anaghị akọwa iko niile?
questions.answer: 4×3=12: efere anọ, iko atọ n’efere ọ bụla, iko iri na abụọ n’ozuzu. 4+3=7 na-agbakwunye ọnụọgụ efere na iko dị n’otu efere; ọ naghị agụ iko dị n’efere anọ niile.
questions.explanation: The multiplication sign models four equal groups. A learner may use3×4 if the interpretation is consistent; the meaningful grouping explanation is essential.

markingGuide.description: Writes a valid multiplication equation yielding12.
Explains four groups of three cups in Igbo.
Names12 cups as the total in Igbo.
Explains why4+3 counts the wrong quantities.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Use multiplication and division symbols for equal groups and equal sharing within 50, explaining their meaning in Igbo.
questions.prompt: Kekọrịta pensụl iri na ise n’etiti ụmụaka atọ ka onye ọ bụla nweta otu ọnụọgụgụ. Dee nke a site n’iji akara ÷. Kọwaa n’Igbo ihe nsonaazụ ahụ pụtara na otú ị ga-esi lelee na nkesa ahụ ziri ezi.
questions.answer: 15÷3=5. Onye ọ bụla nwetara pensụl ise. 3×5=15, ya mere e kesara pensụl niile n’otu n’otu hà nhata.
questions.explanation: The quotient is pencils per child, not the number of children. Equal shares and checking that all fifteen were allocated both matter.

markingGuide.description: Writes15÷3=5.
States in Igbo that each child receives five pencils.
Checks that three equal shares of five account for all15.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Solve and explain original addition or subtraction situations within 50 in Igbo.
questions.prompt: Ada nyere enyi ya pensụl asatọ; pensụl asaa fọdụrụ ya. Pensụl ole ka o nwere tupu o nye enyi ya ụfọdụ? Dee mgbakọ gị, kọwaakwa n’Igbo ihe mere i ji jiri ya mee ihe.
questions.answer: 8+7=15. O nwere pensụl iri na ise: pensụl e nyere na pensụl fọdụrụ bụ pensụl niile o nwere na mbụ.
questions.explanation: Recovering an unknown starting quantity requires joining the removed and remaining quantities; subtracting8 from7 would not represent this situation.

markingGuide.description: Combines the eight given away with the seven remaining.
Gives15 and names the starting total in Igbo.
Explains in Igbo why both parts reconstruct the original set.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Solve and explain original addition or subtraction situations within 50 in Igbo.
questions.prompt: Obi kwuru na 18 − 7 = 12. Lelee okwu ya site n’ịgbakwụnye ọnụọgụgụ o kwuru na nke e wepụrụ. Kọwaa njehie ahụ n’Igbo, deekwa azịza ziri ezi.
questions.answer: 12+7=19, ọ bụghị18. 18−7=11; 11+7=18. Azịza ziri ezi bụ iri na otu.
questions.explanation: An inverse calculation tests the proposed remainder. The explanation must use the check rather than only replace the answer without a reason.

markingGuide.description: Shows12+7=19 and explains why it does not restore18.
Corrects the subtraction to18−7=11.
Checks11+7=18 and explains the correction in Igbo.

questions.prompt: E nwere mkpụrụ mgbakọ isii n’ime igbe. E wepụrụ ha niile. Dee mgbakọ na-egosi ihe mere. Kọwaa n’Igbo ihe 0 pụtara n’akụkọ a.
questions.answer: 6−6=0. Ọ dịghị mkpụrụ mgbakọ fọdụrụ n’ime igbe.
questions.explanation: Removing an entire set leaves none. The learner may explain no items remain without being required to use an unverified single lexical label for zero.

markingGuide.description: Writes6−6=0.
Explains in intelligible Igbo that no counters remain in the box.
